# Independent audit: full-space logarithmic transport and gradient parities

Source read in full: `candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167`, Sections 1–8, including Section 6a. Verdict: **PASS**. No mathematical repair is required. The source verifier was independently rerun: **661 exact rational checks PASS**, including 625 continuous hinge tests. Those checks certify the rational calibration; the analytic existence and parity arguments are audited below.

## 1. Exact hypotheses and feasible separation

The result assumes a genuine attained unpenalized JOINT local minimum in the stated body/parameter class, fixed epsilon, positive continuous concave L on compact canonical C, and Q/M<1/k. This is stronger than stationarity or optimality with respect to L alone. Existence of that setting is supplied by the independently audited logarithmic attainment/positive finite-plane package; it is not established by the transport argument itself.

The radial cone T_L={h: h+cL is concave for some c>=0} is exactly the cone of continuous actual one-sided parameter directions. Its convexity and inclusion of every concave function, both affine signs, and both L signs are correct. Neither this cone nor its finite-dimensional image needs to be closed.

The normalized path derivative is h-L< h/L >. If every proper mark has strictly negative relative derivative, uniform negativity holds in fixed neighborhoods. There, monotonicity controls every nonmaximal mark; at each old maximal mark an attained own-proper cap gives strict loss. Compact attainment of the new maximum supplies a strict proper-base gap. The finite old gaps outside these neighborhoods persist by parameter continuity. Old atomic bases retain the exact weak Q upper bound from their pure-base caps. If equality remains, the separately established actual hinge cleanup makes a further arbitrarily small strict normalized improvement. Both steps fit a prescribed local-minimum neighborhood. This proves the no-strict-negative-image statement without replacing it by a differentiable KKT assertion.

Separation from the OPEN negative orthant gives one nonzero nonnegative sigma. The separating level is zero by cone scaling; normalizing sum sigma=1 is legitimate. The proof does not use a closed-image alternative.

## 2. Measures and actual continuous-target coupling

The signs of mu=sum sigma_i/L_i delta_Yi and nu=dm/(M L) are correct. Both affine signs give identical full mass and first moments. Applying the cone inequality to -phi gives mu<=_cx nu for every continuous convex phi. Both L moments are one. In particular this is a full-space statement, not a discrete base martingale followed by an unjustified conditional-fiber lift.

The row-allocation moment set is compact: allocations are bounded in L2(nu)^s; positivity, upper bounds and sum-one pass under weak convergence; all moment test functions are bounded. Its finite-dimensional separation has precisely the displayed max-of-affines dual, since pointwise allocation to the first maximizing index is measurable. Convex order contradicts this dual separator. Thus the actual q_i exist, preserve every full source barycenter, and sum to the prescribed continuous target law.

Jensen for each row, followed by equality of the total L moments, forces equality row by row. Every active affine majorant therefore has zero nonnegative gap on that entire row. This holds simultaneously for the finite set of planes used subsequently. There is no claim that an arbitrary boundary-base concave function has a finite global supergradient.

## 3. Gradient labels and original mass

For finite-plane L, two active source planes with different continuous gradients would constrain a positive row to a continuous hyperplane of zero d-volume in every fiber. This contradicts absolute continuity and its positive row mass. Hence every positive source has one continuous gradient. Different base gradients are allowed.

Outside finitely many mixed-null hyperplanes, every target also has a unique continuous gradient. The contact identities preserve that gradient along each row. Equation (17) follows from the full row moments. Equation (18) follows by multiplying each row by L and using its preserved L moment. It is exactly an ORIGINAL mixed-volume identity, not merely a tilted-mass equality.

The two equations have different first-moment content: original label mass equals total sigma, whereas the known full first moment is weighted by 1/L. The source explicitly retains this distinction. Positive target labels cannot be absent from the positive source support.

## 4. The midpoint/parity step

The strict atomic depth superlevel is convex: it is the intersection of complements of all closed base halfspaces whose weight is at most Q. This supplies the needed convexity regardless of whether one calls that possibly infinite intersection open. Equal-parity source bases have an integer midpoint in the complete canonical base, and its mark lies in the convex buffered deepest superlevel. Its atomic gap is strict, so it is a proper deepest mark.

At its attained own-proper active cap, the actual upper tail is strictly decreasing near the binding threshold. Every endpoint deepest mark has its threshold at or below that same exact Q-quantile. Averaging these inequalities and using concavity of f forces equality. Strict monotonicity of the positive weighted geometric mean then forces equality in L's midpoint concavity, not merely equality in the product LE.

Every finite plane active at the midpoint consequently touches both endpoints. Their already proved unique continuous gradients agree. A zero sigma at the midpoint causes no difficulty. Thus distinct positive source labels occupy disjoint parity sets. The mass/parity pigeonhole inequality is exactly valid, with no cap credit appended to it.

## 5. Calibration and scope

The rational contact-cell example has the claimed two full-space row means and target law. The forced crease allocations 604/14760 and 44/14760 are recovered directly from the two base first moments; each crease target has mass 648/14760. The respective fractions 151/162 and 11/162 are correct. Uniform continuous rows and the symmetric interval splitting both preserve continuous mean zero. Normalizing L by a constant scales both tilted rows inversely and preserves sigma and all contact identities.

This proves that whole target fibers cannot in general be assigned intact to source contact cells. It is correctly stated as an actual compatibility/quota/transport example, not an attained joint-minimum example.

The audited conclusion is the complete volume transport with its equality contacts and gradient-parity bookkeeping. It does not identify sigma with physical cap-response weights, make gradient-label regions compatible mixed convex bodies, or establish Gamma times label mass/source-parity payment. Those remain separate geometric obligations.
